policy: Observe challenge -> root cause -> generalize -> adapt the owning G0-G16 gate -> add durable regression -> consolidate obsolete checks; never append a new gate merely to remember a lesson.

entries.lesson: Stale certification descendants can continue after a wrapper timeout and contaminate later evidence.
entries.rootCause: Process ownership stopped at the wrapper instead of its descendants.
entries.generalizedRule: Certification timeouts must terminate descendant work and a new fingerprint must start with no stale jobs.

entries.lesson: A gate should not re-execute expensive coverage that is already authoritatively owned by another gate in the same immutable certification.
entries.rootCause: G0 replayed all inherited scope scripts even though G11 separately reruns those exact executable regressions, duplicating work and making baseline verification unnecessarily slow.
entries.generalizedRule: G0 verifies immutable predecessor identity/closure artifacts and learning ownership; G11 is the single executable owner of inherited behavioral revalidation. Coverage is preserved while duplicate heavy execution is consolidated.
permanentProtection: G0 verifies inherited G11 gate presence without executing it
G11 executes every inherited scope gate exactly once per final fingerprint

entries.lesson: Tests must not mutate frozen source or documentation.
entries.rootCause: A regression test wrote README content during randomized execution.
entries.generalizedRule: Certification reads immutable source; test outputs live outside the source tree.

entries.lesson: Exact prose sentinels create false failures when semantics remain correct.
entries.rootCause: Tests coupled safety contracts to one README sentence.
entries.generalizedRule: Assert behavioral/architectural semantics rather than incidental prose except where copy itself is the contract.

entries.lesson: Refactors can leave orphan helpers and duplicate ownership.
entries.rootCause: Temporary helpers survived after consolidation.
entries.generalizedRule: Every build preserves one canonical implementation per responsibility and zero orphan production helpers.

entries.lesson: Release manifests and file-count metadata must reflect frozen artifacts, not stale summaries.
entries.rootCause: A prior delivery lost the standalone manifest and carried a stale ZIP file count.
entries.generalizedRule: Count the actual final ZIP, generate SHA manifest LAST, then verify every entry.

entries.lesson: Stable promotion must preserve compatible credentials/settings.
entries.rootCause: TEST runtime isolation used a different Application Support directory.
entries.generalizedRule: Stable releases use PersonalMarketTerminal and verify prior Stable secrets continuity before authorization.

entries.lesson: Historical replay must not leak current state and outcome ordering must respect entry before target.
entries.rootCause: Present caches and coarse historical ordering can contaminate retrospective validation.
entries.generalizedRule: Replay is cutoff-isolated; what was known then is frozen before outcomes are measured.

entries.lesson: Daily completed-bar truth cannot use the next observed bar timestamp across weekends/holidays.
entries.rootCause: Gap duration was mistaken for bar duration.
entries.generalizedRule: Completed evidence uses canonical timeframe duration and session truth.

entries.lesson: Heavy race/randomized/responsive work can create false failures under host contention.
entries.rootCause: Unbounded parallel heavy jobs competed for CPU/browser resources.
entries.generalizedRule: LIGHT <=4, MEDIUM <=2, HEAVY normally 1 with explicit bounded sharding.

entries.lesson: Product readiness and build-host capability are separate truths.
entries.rootCause: Unavailable host-native/security tooling was conflated with product defects.
entries.generalizedRule: Report host/native residuals explicitly without hiding them in app startup or mislabeling product failures.

entries.lesson: Active documentation terminology must follow the current release model.
entries.rootCause: Old TEST wording survived a Stable policy change.
entries.generalizedRule: G16 validates active WC/RC/Stable terminology while preserving historical release records as history.

entries.lesson: Application bundle naming is a user-facing release contract.
entries.rootCause: A temporary De-Pulse-stable.app name was treated as if it were standard.
entries.generalizedRule: macOS Stable bundle is /Applications/De-Pulse.app; release labels belong in version/build metadata, not the app name.

entries.lesson: Randomized certification runners must not hard-code a previous release seed whitelist.
entries.rootCause: The G12 runner embedded v16.3-only argparse choices, so valid v16.4 plan seeds were rejected before tests executed.
entries.generalizedRule: The certification plan owns reproducible release seeds; the generic G12 runner validates only safe positive seed shape and remains version-agnostic.

entries.lesson: Full-minor documentation governance must include the repository top-level README current-release identity, not only in-app Documentation tabs.
entries.rootCause: v16.4 canonical User/Developer/Limitations docs were current while README still called v16.3 the current Stable baseline.
entries.generalizedRule: G16 validates README version/build/scope/app-identity/learning truth alongside in-app canonical docs before RC authorization.

entries.lesson: Stored QA/release history must not fail simply because valid release history grows beyond an old fixed test count.
entries.rootCause: renderer_logic_test.js imposed an obsolete <=10 cap on an append-only manifest even though the UI intentionally renders only the latest five entries.
entries.generalizedRule: Release history is monotonic and append-only; tests validate current-first metadata and independently validate bounded recent-history presentation instead of capping stored history.
permanentProtection: renderer logic asserts append-only manifest without a maximum-count sentinel
qaHistoryMarkup independently limits visible history with slice(0,5)
G16 validates current release first in manifest

entries.lesson: Responsive tests for continuously animated UI must track element identity instead of assuming the element remains under a fixed screen coordinate.
entries.rootCause: The ticker hover regression required animation to remain running, then used elementFromPoint at the pre-animation coordinate; at one viewport the correctly moving item left that coordinate and produced a false null failure.
entries.generalizedRule: Animated-component geometry tests bind to the original DOM element/index and independently assert animation state; fixed-coordinate hit-testing is not used to identify a moving target after time advances.
permanentProtection: responsive_ui_test.py tracks ticker item index across animation
hover geometry and animation-play-state remain separate assertions

entries.lesson: Persisted collection state must distinguish an intentionally empty list from a missing/legacy list.
entries.rootCause: Master Symbol last-item removal serialized/normalized an empty desk slice as nil; legacy normalization interpreted nil as a missing watchlist and restored defaults.
entries.generalizedRule: For persisted user-owned collections, nil may represent legacy/missing state only; explicit empty state must remain non-nil through mutation, normalization, save, reload and public rendering.
permanentProtection: Master Symbol Store UI separates user-managed symbols from protected market context

entries.lesson: Current-release UI/test fixtures must not hard-code a previous release version/build literal.
entries.rootCause: Current-release renderer logic and responsive fixtures had duplicated release literals; renderer logic was generalized first, but responsive_ui_test.py still injected the previous v16.5 build-name suffix and falsely reported a v16.6 build-identity mismatch.
entries.generalizedRule: Every current-release UI/test fixture derives version/build from the canonical packaged renderer identity owner and then asserts all surfaces agree; historical release literals remain explicit only when history itself is under test.
permanentProtection: responsive_ui_test.py derives canonical renderer identity for primary and scaling fixtures
version_consistency_test.py remains the canonical cross-surface identity gate

entries.lesson: Roadmap item IDs/names alone do not preserve the original approved acceptance depth.
entries.rootCause: A later implementation can narrow a capability while retaining the same roadmap ID/name, allowing evolved traceability to report 30/30 even when original sub-requirements are partial.
entries.generalizedRule: Every roadmap item carries immutable original_acceptance clauses. G1 freezes them, G11 executes behavioral proof against them, and G16 reports FULL/PARTIAL/MISSING/DEFERRED/EXPLICITLY_AMENDED. Scope reductions require explicit user approval.
permanentProtection: current-release scope gate validates original acceptance clauses
final roadmap audit reports clause-level status

entries.lesson: A timeout during Go test enumeration is infrastructure evidence, not automatically a product race failure.
entries.rootCause: An independent v16.6 audit saw go test -list exceed a 45-second wrapper limit before any race test ran; immediate isolated reruns and the complete second certification passed.
entries.generalizedRule: G12 distinguishes enumeration/setup timeout from a race/test failure, preserves the first incident, retries enumeration once after stale-job checks, and only classifies a reproducible race/test failure as PRODUCT FAIL.
permanentProtection: explicit INFRASTRUCTURE FAIL classification after repeated enumeration timeout
race shard PASS requires actual -race execution

entries.lesson: Canonical in-app documentation titles must remain the first Markdown heading even when a release-specific update is added.
entries.rootCause: The v16.8 documentation update prepended release-note headings above the canonical User/Developer documentation titles. G12 renderer logic correctly rejected the changed first-line contract.
entries.generalizedRule: Release-specific documentation updates are inserted below the canonical document title; canonical role/audience headings remain first-line identity and are protected by renderer/documentation gates.
permanentProtection: renderer_logic_test.js asserts canonical User/Developer documentation first-line titles
release updates are nested below canonical document identity rather than replacing it

entries.lesson: Current-release end-to-end HTTP workflow assertions must derive release identity from the canonical version owner rather than retaining the predecessor Stable literal.
entries.rootCause: The v16.8 product correctly reported version/build 16.8.0, but http_workflow_test.py still asserted v16.7.0 and therefore produced a blocking false failure after source freeze.
entries.generalizedRule: Any current-release HTTP/integration fixture derives expected version and build identity from VERSION.txt (or the canonical packaged identity owner). Historical release assertions remain explicit only when historical compatibility itself is under test.
permanentProtection: http_workflow_test.py derives EXPECTED_VERSION and EXPECTED_BUILD_ID from VERSION.txt
HTTP workflow verifies current health/bootstrap/maintenance/renderer identity against the canonical release owner
current release traceability is explicitly exercised while prior traceability remains historical compatibility evidence

entries.lesson: Machine-readable release metadata can drift even when runtime/version tests pass.
entries.rootCause: ci_pipeline_plan.json retained an older version/baseline because release identity was duplicated across independent files.
entries.generalizedRule: One canonical release identity owns current version/build/baseline/channel; all release-owned metadata is generated or semantically verified against it before freeze.
permanentProtection: current-state professional/test fixtures derive canonical release identity

entries.lesson: Cheap release-truth failures discovered after RC freeze create avoidable full-certification restart cost.
entries.rootCause: Documentation identity and HTTP current-release identity were validated too late in v16.8 heavy certification.
entries.generalizedRule: A candidate must pass pre-freeze qualification for identity/docs/renderer/HTTP smoke/source health/scope/data utility before immutable G12 heavy certification.

entries.lesson: Inherited renderer acceptance must protect enduring capability semantics without pinning superseded UI filters or current-release identity literals.
entries.rootCause: The first v16.8.1 frozen RC passed current renderer qualification but historical v16.7/v16.8 renderer scripts still asserted the old Region calendar control and exact v16.8.0 current-release identity, creating blocking false regressions after freeze.
entries.generalizedRule: Historical renderer gates assert enduring capability/invariant semantics and are included in pre-freeze qualification. Current-release identity is owned only by the canonical identity/version gates; historical UI literals may remain only when that exact historical compatibility contract is intentionally under test.
permanentProtection: v16_7_renderer_test.js follows evolved US/Global Context calendar semantics
v16_8_renderer_test.js checks canonical identity hook rather than a superseded current-release value

entries.lesson: A release scope gate must not recursively own expensive inherited certification that already has an independent evidence owner.
entries.rootCause: The first v16.10 scope-gate composition invoked the complete v16.9 30/30 audit as a child process. Under captured orchestration this coupled unrelated checkpoints and exceeded wrapper limits even though the inherited audit passed standalone.
entries.generalizedRule: Execute each unique evidence-producing regression once per fingerprint as an independent checkpointed job. Scope gates consume/reference that evidence and run only release-specific acceptance plus bounded invariants; do not recursively nest another heavy certification/audit suite.
permanentProtection: prefreeze_qualification.py owns v16.9 original roadmap audit as an independent job
certification_plan.json gives inherited roadmap audit its own checkpoint

entries.lesson: Parallel CI/CD scheduling must account for shared toolchain/build-cache resource classes, not only logical dependency independence.
entries.rootCause: v16.10 pre-freeze initially ran Go vet/full-Go and other Go-heavy evidence in the same parallel medium wave. Although logically independent, they contend for Go build/cache/CPU resources and made wrapper completion less reliable.
entries.generalizedRule: Executable DAG jobs declare resource class. Go/build-cache-heavy certification jobs run in a controlled lane unless capacity evidence proves safe concurrency; independent I/O/HTTP/professional checks may use bounded parallelism.
permanentProtection: certification process metrics track wall time and wrapper interruptions

entries.lesson: A major-family transition cannot be authorized from accumulated release reports alone.
entries.rootCause: Incremental builds can each pass their local scope while cross-release drift, stale assumptions or weak inherited evidence remain hidden unless the final current source is freshly inspected and exercised as one system.
entries.generalizedRule: Before every major-version jump, run a mandatory Major Closure & Release Assurance build that reconstructs the outgoing family scope from immutable contracts, maps it to current code owners, executes fresh behavioral evidence, performs expert engineering and real-money acceptance, and issues an explicit GO/NO-GO.

entries.lesson: Correctly labeling market data as STALE is insufficient if downstream decision-readiness can still remain READY.
entries.rootCause: Quote freshness truth and Trade Readiness severity were evaluated in separate paths; stale current-price evidence did not automatically raise readiness severity when broader Market Tradeability was normal.
entries.generalizedRule: Real-money acceptance must cross-check data-state truth against every decision surface. STALE/CACHED/HISTORY-ONLY current-price evidence cannot present a clean Day entry readiness state; safety overlays may lower readiness but never mutate protected deterministic score formulas.

entries.lesson: Historical release documents and build debris do not belong in the runtime source package merely because they were once useful during development.
entries.rootCause: An obsolete v16.1 TEST handoff DOCX remained at source root even though no production/test/package consumer referenced it.
entries.generalizedRule: Major closure audits source-package hygiene. Non-source artifacts require an explicit retained-asset purpose/consumer; superseded release documents stay in authoritative release/library history instead of current runtime source.

entries.lesson: A desktop persistence foundation is not complete until every supported packaged OS uses the promised canonical storage technology rather than a silent compatibility fallback.
entries.rootCause: The first v17.0 SQLite implementation used native SQLite on macOS/Linux but could fall back to JSON on Windows/CGO-disabled builds, violating the frozen cross-platform persistence contract even though primary-host tests were green.
entries.generalizedRule: Platform parity is an architectural acceptance property. Cross-compile/backend-selection gates must prove the same persistence truth model on every supported desktop target before a persistence slice can qualify.

entries.lesson: A conservative upstream data-quality state must not be multiplied downstream into many apparently independent market-risk exceptions.
entries.rootCause: Market Open Prep converted stale/missing quote-derived conservative liquidity states into per-symbol LIQUIDITY RISK cards even though Quotes freshness already owned the shared stale root cause.
entries.generalizedRule: Preserve root-cause semantics across transformations: stale/incomplete evidence stays a freshness/data-quality problem unless current market evidence independently proves the derived market risk. Group repeated genuine causes without hiding per-symbol drill-down.

entries.lesson: Release governance must distinguish the current TEST/RC identity from the latest authoritative Stable baseline during a major-family build.
entries.rootCause: Inherited documentation/version gates assumed the current manifest entry itself must remain v16.11 Stable, creating false failures once legitimate v17 TEST checkpoints became current.
entries.generalizedRule: Canonical current identity may advance through TEST/RC while a separate Stable-baseline invariant protects the last certified Stable until promotion. Historical gates verify preserved behavior rather than pinning predecessor current-version literals.
permanentProtection: historical v17 slice gates accept later v17.x TEST identity

entries.lesson: Consolidation is incomplete if superseded production owners/helpers are left behind merely because tests still reference them.
entries.rootCause: v17.4 initially left a duplicate Master Market Symbols renderer and then exposed an obsolete liquidity wrapper as test-only orphan code after callers moved to the canonical context-aware owner.
entries.generalizedRule: REUSE/CONSOLIDATE/REFACTOR/DELETE before ADD includes deleting superseded production owners and updating tests to the canonical owner. Do not whitelist dead helpers to satisfy source-health gates.
permanentProtection: single Master Market Symbols renderer assertion

entries.lesson: Pre-freeze qualification must not serialize historical scope gates that recursively rerun regression families already owned by current fingerprint-scoped jobs.
entries.rootCause: The v17 Major Closure pre-freeze MEDIUM-GO lane still invoked v16.1-v16.10 scope gates whose implementations reran overlapping Go, renderer and deterministic evidence. Coverage was preserved but orchestration wall time and wrapper exposure grew dramatically.
entries.generalizedRule: At major closure, static/current scope matrices prove historical scope mapping while each unique behavioral family executes once through its authoritative current-source owner. Historical recursive gates remain available for diagnosis but are not stacked into the normal pre-freeze DAG.
permanentProtection: full Go + inherited renderer + professional jobs remain independently blocking

entries.lesson: Baseline provenance gates must validate the predecessor Stable anchor independently from the current candidate channel.
entries.rootCause: The v17 baseline gate correctly protected v16.11 provenance but also hard-coded channel TEST, so the legitimate v17.5 RC closure candidate failed G0 even though its predecessor Stable, SHA, clean fingerprint and v16→v17 GO anchors were unchanged.
entries.generalizedRule: A major-family baseline gate verifies immutable predecessor provenance and permits the current family through its approved candidate lifecycle (TEST → RC). Stable promotion remains a separate release-authorization step; do not conflate candidate channel with predecessor authority.
permanentProtection: Major Closure certification runner G0 baseline check

entries.lesson: Stable promotion is incomplete if runtime identity or current in-app documentation still describes the promoted build as RC/TEST or omits completed delivery slices.
entries.rootCause: v17.5 promoted exact certified RC bits after native acceptance, but G16 did not require post-promotion reconciliation of runtime channel/build copy or complete v17.0-v17.5 user-facing history.
entries.generalizedRule: A Stable promotion must reconcile canonical runtime/renderer identity and current user-facing documentation to Stable truth while preserving historical checkpoint evidence separately. Major-slice history completeness is a release-governance acceptance property.
